rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.4, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=20, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=REGIME-BOUND CONFIRMATION replay of the best config (NFE8, init_t0.4, eta1.0, n_cg20, dc_relax1.0; PSNR~28.91/RMSE~0.0122), fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_unconstrained breast val=200. All 5 sampler/DC axes exhausted (dc_relax 0.5/1.0, init_t 0.7/0.4/0.2, n_cg 5/20/60, NFE 8/16, eta 1.0/0.5): recon pinned ~7.4 dB below the 128-view sparse-FBP floor (PSNR36.32/RMSE0.0052), hr=0 throughout. Root cause: the MAYO-trained WDM-wavelet prior (baked fd_out_scale=0.05 vs breast mu->0.5, a 10x normaliser mismatch) adds no useful structure and the discrete per-Euler-step CG data-consistency (8 injections) cannot match the analytic sparse-FBP inversion; pushing CG just amplifies sparse-view noise. Honest below-baseline finding for the UNconstrained (Mayo-fallback) wavelet prior on sparse breast. Banking the confirmation toward the required 20 valid iters.

rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=15, gs_n_gaussians=1024, gs_n_iter=130, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=True, gs_render=raster, gs_ssim_weight=0.3, seed=42, train_n=0, rationale=iter-14 (search-20260703-01) -- CEILING CONFIRMATION #6. SIX-BOX: hr pinned 0 at EVERY prior iter; best SSIM 0.9278 @ iter-6. R2-Gaussian is REGIME-BOUNDED on dense 128-view breast: the coarse anisotropic-Gaussian basis (1024 splats, 0.006M params) plateaus at SSIM ~0.928 / PSNR ~28.7 dB, ~7.3 dB BELOW the 128-view FBP baseline (PSNR 35.97), so the RMSE/PSNR-gated headroom stays 0 (reproduces findings.md 2026-06-03). All 7 lever families mapped+exhausted (steps FLAT, capacity +0.010, warm-start +0.039, SSIM-loss +0.073, SSIM-weight saturated, basis-scale FLAT, TV-reg FLAT); NONE moves hr off 0 -- the strongest (warm-start + SSIM-loss) got closest but stayed 7.3 dB short. The R2-G paper's regime is SPARSE-view CBCT (<=50 views) where FBP is weak; dense 128-view 2D CT is the wrong inductive bias. DECISION: empty-patch re-run of the iter-6 run-best config (warm-start + SSIM-loss@0.30, 1024G/130it) to confirm SSIM ~0.928 / hr=0 reproduces. BUDGET: ~660-1000s node-dependent, under the 1080 in-solver wall and 1800 SLURM wall, figure excluded. val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT. PREDICTION: SSIM ~0.928 (0.925-0.930), hr 0 -- faithful-but-regime-bounded negative result., gs_outer_wall_s=1080, gs_amp_init_max=0.05

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, img_sx=2.5, img_sy=2.5, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-9 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: image BF SPATIAL sigma img_sx=img_sy 1.5->2.5 (isotropic widen), on iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, n_iter=30). n_iter REVERTED to 30 (iter-8 n_iter=100 gave hr=0.1160 on a wall-trimmed val_n=193/harder-baseline subset; SSIM/PSNR were actually higher 0.9620/39.72 but n_iter did not clearly help and it trims the val set -> keep 30 for a clean 200-scene comparison). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 (img_sr=0.0002). HYPOTHESIS: with the range kernel now EDGE-PRESERVING (tight img_sr), a WIDER spatial sigma lets each output pixel average over MORE same-tissue neighbours -> stronger flat-region noise suppression, while the tight range kernel still BLOCKS averaging across fibroglandular edges -> cleaner denoise WITHOUT new blur -> hr climbs above 0.1261. This is the direction that lifted the DEMO bilateral monotonically (1.5->2.5->3.5); the question is whether it transfers to breast NOW that range-edge-preservation is on (on the OLD-split breast it barely moved because range was not this tight). If hr FLAT/DROPS, breast's fine fibroglandular structure sits inside the widened window and even edge-guarded spatial widening blurs it -> spatial axis capped at 1.5. BUDGET: spatial-sigma cost is independent of VALUE (same 7x7 kernel unfold); ~700-1000s like iter-7. ONE knob: img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5.

rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=15, gs_n_gaussians=1024, gs_n_iter=130, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=True, gs_render=raster, gs_ssim_weight=0.3, seed=42, train_n=0, rationale=iter-12 (search-20260703-01) -- CEILING CONFIRMATION #4. DECISION: empty-patch re-run of the iter-6 run-best config (warm-start + SSIM-loss@0.30, 1024G/130it) to confirm SSIM ~0.928 / hr=0 reproduces. rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=100, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-8 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: per-scene steps n_iter 30->100, on the iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 SSIM0.9606 PSNR39.57 (img_sr 0.0005->0.0002 marginal +0.0004 over iter-5's 0.1257; range-sigma optimum is flat ~2e-4..5e-4). HYPOTHESIS: iter-1/iter-3 showed n_iter did NOT help when img_sr was WIDE (0.02) -- more steps just pulled the over-smoothing BF further toward the blurry 64-view half-target. But now img_sr is TIGHT/edge-preserving, so additional per-scene N2I steps should refine the edge-preserving denoiser toward better noise suppression WITHOUT over-blurring (the tight range kernel structurally cannot cross edges regardless of step count) -> hr climbs above 0.1261. If hr FLAT/DROPS, the edge-preserving BF converges fast (30 steps already enough) and n_iter is saturated -> revert to 30 and move to spatial sigma. FAILURE watched: even edge-preserving, too many steps could still creep the recon toward the noisy half-target mean (mild PSNR drop). BUDGET: n_iter 30->100 ~3.3x inner steps; iter-7 ran 692s at n_iter30 on a fast node but iter-1 n_iter120 was 1200s -> n_iter100 ~1000-1100s; outer_wall_s=900 caps it (may trim a few scenes). ONE knob: n_iter 30->100.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=False, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=300, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-4 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-3 hr=0.0, unet_c=32 (4x capacity) gave rmse=0.00654 (SLIGHTLY WORSE than c=16's 0.00638), ssim=0.932, 196/200. So higher denoiser capacity does NOT sharpen -- capacity is NOT the limiter. Iters 1-3 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity) all pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: structural over-smoothing from the poor 128-view FBP self-supervision target, independent of budget or capacity. (3) ONE KNOB: warm_start True -> False (back to c=16). Pure per-image N2I: each val scan is optimized FROM SCRATCH on its own sinogram with NO amortised train-set pre-pass init; n_iter raised to 300 to compensate for losing the warm init (this is the SAME knob -- turning off the amortised init -- expressed as the from-scratch regime it defines; no train split is loaded at all). (4) HYPOTHESIS: removing the amortised warm-start tests whether the pre-pass was pulling every scan toward an over-smoothed mean. If pure per-image N2I clears hr>0, warm-start was the culprit. Per the documented ceiling, more likely each from-scratch fit STILL converges to the same over-smoothed FBP-consistent solution (hr=0), because the ceiling is set by the self-supervision TARGET, not the initialization. (5) BUDGET: no warm-start pre-pass (SAVES ~130s), so the full 1400s outer wall goes to the 200 per-image fits at 7.0s each; c=16 + figure ~= 24 min < 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-5 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: pretrain_epochs (stronger warm-start), lr up/down, n_iter early-stop, unet_c=8.

HYPOTHESIS: the SAME edge-preserving fix in the PROJECTION domain (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) suppresses sparse-view streak noise in the sinogram before FBP WITHOUT the view-inconsistency that a strong-but-wide proj filter causes (findings.md: keep proj filtering gentle/soft -- a tight RANGE sigma is soft-edged in intensity, exactly the recommended lever) -> hr climbs above 0.1257. If hr drops vs iter-5, proj-domain edge-preservation induces view inconsistency and the image domain alone is the safe lever. BUDGET: value change only, ~1020s like iter-5. ONE knob: proj_sr 0.02->0.0005.

All 5 sampler/DC axes exhausted (dc_relax 0.5/1.0, init_t 0.7/0.4/0.2, n_cg 5/20/60, NFE 8/16, eta 1.0/0.5): recon pinned ~7.4 dB below the 128-view sparse-FBP floor (PSNR36.32/RMSE0.0052), hr=0 throughout. Root cause: the MAYO-trained WDM-wavelet prior (baked fd_out_scale=0.05 vs breast mu->0.5, a 10x normaliser mismatch) adds no useful structure and the discrete per-Euler-step CG data-consistency (8 injections) cannot match the analytic sparse-FBP inversion; pushing CG just amplifies sparse-view noise. Base = iter-4 BEST (warm-start ON, 1024 Gaussians / 130 it -- the run-best config). The SSIM term needs an FBP target, which warm-start provides. PRIOR NUMBERS: iter-1 0.8032 (cold 512G/150it), iter-2 0.8048 (512G/220it, steps FLAT), iter-3 0.8145 (1024G/130it, capacity +0.010), iter-4 0.8539 (warm-start, BEST, +0.039, PSNR 22.50). hr pinned 0 at EVERY iter -- even the best config (warm-start) sits PSNR 22.50 vs 128-view FBP baseline 35.97 (a 13.5 dB gap) -> hr=0. FAILURE MODE: the coarse anisotropic-Gaussian basis cannot reconstruct dense breast soft tissue near the strong sparse-FBP baseline; warm-start gave the biggest lift (it literally seeds from FBP) yet stays far below the FBP floor on the PSNR/RMSE-gated headroom. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): a pure-L2 loss ignores the SSIM the metric rewards; adding an SSIM pull toward FBP structure lifts SSIM above iter-4 0.8539. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.8539 (no lift), the SSIM-loss lever is exhausted. hr expected 0 regardless (matching FBP PSNR 35.97 with a 1024-Gaussian mixture is implausible, and SSIM-weight typically TRADES PSNR DOWN -- the headroom gate is PSNR/RMSE-based, so it cannot move hr off 0). val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT (gs_outer_wall_s=1080). BUDGET: SSIM term = 1 cheap conv/step vs the dominating projection -> same ~990s as iter-4 << 1080 wall. TRAJECTORY: iter-4 0.8539 (warm-start, BEST) -> iter-5 SSIM-loss @0.15 test., gs_outer_wall_s=1080, gs_amp_init_max=0.05

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=True, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-6 (breast_ct). SHARED-STEP probe (parametrisation family). iters 1-5: step (1e-2/1e-4/1e-3), depth (K=50), loss (l1) ALL collapse the K independent step[k]->~0 -> recon = FBP init, hr0. NAMED failure: with K INDEPENDENT step/lambda scalars the optimiser can zero out every step to sit on the MSE-optimal FBP fixed point. HYPOTHESIS: tv_share_steps=true collapses the 20 scalars to 2 (ONE step + ONE lambda shared across all K=10 iters). A single shared step cannot be selectively zeroed per-iter; to reduce the supervised loss AT ALL via TV it must commit to one non-zero step that does denoising across all 10 iters -- which may find a net-beneficial smoothing the per-iter version escaped. ONE KNOB: tv_share_steps false->true (step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3, K=10, mse -- all reverted to the iter-3 base to isolate the sharing knob). FALSIFIER: if the single shared step ALSO -> 0 and hr stays 0, the FBP fixed point is a parametrisation-agnostic MSE attractor -> confirms the structural ceiling (findings 2026-05-23). BUDGET: K=10 mse ~750s like iter-3, <1200s wall.

rationale: fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_constrained-claude-agentic: val_n=200, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_wavelet_constrained.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.7, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=1.0, dataset_kind=breast_ct, rationale=iter-2 fastdiff_wdm_wavelet_constrained breast (search-20260703-01), val_n=200. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) PRIOR: iter-1 (dc_relax0.5, init_t0.7, steps8, eta1.0) -> SSIM 0.7220, PSNR 27.35, RMSE 1.465e-2, hr 0.0000, elapsed 121s. Breast LD-FBP calibrated baseline_PSNR ~36.3 (baseline is a STRONG sparse-view FBP after calibration); the Mayo-trained wavelet prior (fd_out_scale=0.05) is ~10x mis-normalised vs breast mu~0.5, so at dc_relax=0.5 only HALF the CG-projected (data-consistent) image is blended in and the mis-scaled prior half drags PSNR ~9 dB below baseline -> hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: prior-domain-normalisation mismatch corrupts HU faster than the PARTIAL (relax0.5) DC pulls it back; the DC-strength axis is under-applied. (3) ONE KNOB: fd_recon_dc_relax 0.5 -> 1.0 (FULL hard-CG DC projection each Euler step; blend the CG-fit image 100%, discard the mis-scaled prior's HU offset). ALL else identical to iter-1 (steps8, init_t0.7, eta1.0, dc1, n_cg5). This is the proven Mayo-constrained RMSE-down direction (its iter-2->3 dc_relax0.5->1.0 lowered RMSE). (4) HYPOTHESIS: dc_relax 0.5->1.0 lifts PSNR toward the FBP baseline and cuts RMSE below 1.465e-2 because full DC anchors every slice to its measured 128-view sinogram, neutralising the 10x out_scale prior mismatch; hr may still be 0 (a Mayo-prior on breast is FBP-bounded) but RMSE must drop meaningfully. FALSIFIER: if RMSE >= 1.465e-2 (dc_relax INERT or worse), full DC is already saturated at relax0.5 -> iter-3 pivots to fd_recon_init_t lower (0.7->0.4, start reverse-diffusion closer to FBP so the mis-scaled prior has fewer steps to drift HU). (5) BUDGET: dc_relax is FREE (same 8 steps + CG5); iter-1 ran 121s << 1200s budget / 1800s kill. val=ALL 200 seed-20260703 cases. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing via the numeric-RMSE gate.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=200, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=32, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-2 hr=0.0, val_rmse=0.00638 (baseline 0.00521), val_ssim=0.942, 198/200 scans -- essentially IDENTICAL to iter-1's 0.00640 despite +55% per-scene budget (7.0s vs 4.5s). So MORE inner N2I optimization does NOT lower RMSE: the iter-1 plateau was NOT under-fitting. (2) FAILURE MODE: structural over-smoothing -- the N2I self-supervision target (128-view FBP split into two half-view subsets) is itself too poor to push recon RMSE below the full-view sparse FBP baseline, regardless of how long each scan is fit. (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 16 -> 32 (both denoisers; ~4x params, 0.466M -> ~1.86M). Everything else identical to iter-2. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a higher-capacity denoiser pair is more expressive and MIGHT sharpen edges the c=16 net blurred; if hr rises above 0 that identifies capacity as the bottleneck. More likely (per the documented ceiling) the extra capacity just fits the noisy FBP target more faithfully and hr STAYS 0, showing capacity is not the limiter -- the SUPERVISION TARGET is. (5) BUDGET: c=32 is ~2-3x slower per step so per_scene=7.0s fits fewer inner iters, but warm-start ep=3 + 200*7.0s loop + figure ~= 26 min < 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-4 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: warm_start off (pure per-image), pretrain_epochs, lr, n_iter early-stop, unet_c=8.

Prior ckpt = MAYO-TRAINED fast_diffusion_wavelet_constrained.pt (domain=wavelet mode=constrained ch=64 fd_out_scale=0.05 val_flow_loss=0.0174) -- NO breast-native wavelet prior exists, so this is the documented Mayo-prior fallback; breast mu ranges to ~0.5 (10x Mayo's ~0.05 out_scale normaliser) so a domain-normalisation mismatch is EXPECTED and the DC-step is what anchors HU. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: none for this slug; nearest ref = Mayo fastdiff-wdm-wavelet-CONSTRAINED search-20260620-01 (all 20 iters hr=0, regime-bound below the 2304-view dense-Mayo FBP floor; its best converged at steps16/init_t0.4/dc_relax1.0, SSIM~0.915 RMSE~1.23e-3). Its constrained sibling curve showed lower init_t + full dc_relax was the RMSE-down direction. Breast is the OPPOSITE regime: 128-view SPARSE, where the wavelet prior + hard CG DC-step is designed to help MOST (data under-constrains, the prior fills the null space and DC pins the measured rays). (2) FAILURE MODE: N/A onboarding; goal = does the DC-constrained wavelet recon RUN on breast 128-view 512^2 val=200 under the HARD 20-min budget and where does it sit vs the sparse-view FBP baseline (breast LD-FBP baseline_PSNR ~36.3)? rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=l1, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-5 (breast_ct). LOSS-FORMULATION probe. iters 1-4 mapped step (1e-2 diverge, 1e-4/1e-3 collapse-to-FBP) and depth (K=50 also collapses) -- under MSE the optimiser ALWAYS drives step[k]->0 and sits on the FBP init (psnr~36.3=baseline, hr0, loss floor ~0.00624 = FBP's own MSE). NAMED failure: FBP-init is an MSE-optimal attractor -- TV smoothing trades pixel-MSE for perceptual quality, so a pixel-MSE loss has NO incentive to move off FBP. HYPOTHESIS: an L1 loss weights outliers (the sparse-view streak/noise residual in FBP) differently from MSE and is NOT minimised by staying exactly at FBP -- so the optimiser keeps step non-zero and does real streak/noise removal, moving val metrics off the FBP floor and clearing hr>0. ONE KNOB: loss_base mse -> l1 (K=10, step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3 kept from iter-3; K reverted 50->10 to isolate the loss knob and fit budget). All else identical. FALSIFIER: if L1 also collapses step->0 and hr stays 0, the FBP-init attractor is loss-agnostic on dense-view breast -> the supervised-unrolled-TV skeleton cannot beat FBP here regardless of loss (matches findings 2026-05-23) and I pivot to lambda/architecture knobs. BUDGET: K=10 -> ~750s like iter-3, well under 1200s wall.

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=50, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (breast_ct). DEPTH probe. iter-1/2/3 mapped the step axis: 1e-2 diverges (hr0), 1e-4 and 1e-3 both COLLAPSE the learned step to ~0 so the K=10 recon sits on the FBP init (psnr~36.3=baseline, hr0). NAMED failure: at K=10 the optimiser prefers step->0 because FBP-init already has MSE-optimal psnr 36.3 and 10 TV steps cannot out-denoise it, so staying put minimises the supervised MSE. KEY CONTRAST: the classical (non-learned) tv_iterative sibling BEATS FBP on this exact split (hr 0.16 at 200 iters -> 0.355 at 1000 iters) using the SAME TV iteration but with MANY iterations at fixed non-zero step/lambda -- it does real iterative denoising that K=10 cannot reach. HYPOTHESIS: the limiter is UNROLL DEPTH, not step scale -- with enough steps the TV iteration can denoise the FBP noise below FBP's own MSE, giving the optimiser a reason to KEEP step non-zero. ONE KNOB: tv_K 10 -> 50 (5x depth; step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3 kept from iter-3). All else identical. EXPECT: step[k] no longer collapses to 0, recon departs FBP with net denoising, val_psnr rises above 36.3 and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step still collapses to 0 and hr stays 0, depth is NOT the limiter and the FBP fixed point is a hard supervised-MSE attractor at any K (matches findings 2026-05-23 verdict) -> iter-5 switches loss (l1) or attacks lambda. BUDGET: iter-3 ran ~750s at K=10; K=50 is 5x the unrolled fwd/bwd in BOTH train and val. Train ~5x, val ~5x -> est ~ (750-load)*~3 + load. Conservatively ~900-1100s; still under the 1200s wall. If it risks the wall iter-5 trims val_n or epochs.

Lambda peak located at 2.5e-3 (iter-8 hr=0.36286 best; 2e-3->0.3552, 3e-3->0.3597). Earlier convergence logs showed the TV term still descending at iter-1000 under plain GD (data term converged) => the TV minimum may be under-converged by GD. ONE knob: tv_optimizer gd->adam (keep lambda=2.5e-3, 1000 iters, lr=0.01, decay=0.01, fbp). HYPOTHESIS: Adam's adaptive per-parameter steps reach a deeper TV minimum than plain GD in 1000 iters so hr rises past 0.36286; if Adam at lr=0.01 overshoots/destabilizes the data term (hr collapses) GD is required and I revert then tune lr/decay. (Note: manhart's adam@lr=0.01 collapsed hr->0 on the same TV core — this is a genuine independent test on plain TV.) Budget: ~950s at 1000 iters, <1200s wall.

HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): if doubling the basis (512->1024 Gaussians) lifts SSIM materially above 0.8048 / RMSE below 0.03172, capacity is the binding limiter and more splats help. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.80 flat (or drops), the basis-coarseness ceiling is confirmed as capacity-insensitive in this budget -- 1024 splats still land far below the FBP floor on PSNR/RMSE (hr=0). Prior findings (1024 G at 10k-40k iters -> hr=0) predict FLAT. val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT (gs_outer_wall_s=1080). rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-3 (breast_ct). BRACKET the step regime. iter-1 (step=1e-2): OVERSHOOT -> diverged 19 dB below FBP, hr=0. iter-2 (step=1e-4): training un-froze BUT the optimiser drove step[k] DOWN to ~6e-7 (a near-no-op), so the recon converged to EXACTLY the LD-FBP init (val_psnr 36.31 vs baseline 36.32, ssim 0.9198 vs 0.9199) -> hr=0. NAMED failure mode: FBP-INIT ZERO-GRADIENT TRAP (findings 2026-05-23) -- since R+ ~= FBP, the data-gradient R^T(R*FBP - g) ~= 0 at init, so the supervised loss's only signal is stay-put; too-small a step lets it sit on FBP, too-large a step diverges. The productive regime is BETWEEN 1e-4 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-4 -> 1e-3 (geometric midpoint of the bracket; 10x iter-2, 10x below the iter-1 overshoot). All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200). HYPOTHESIS: at step=1e-3 the unrolled TV iteration is large enough to move the recon OFF the FBP fixed point and do real denoising work, yet small enough to stay in the stable basin (no divergence), so val_psnr rises ABOVE the FBP floor (>36.3 dB) and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step=1e-3 also diverges (like 1e-2) the stable band is narrow -> iter-4 bisects toward 3e-4; if it again collapses to FBP (step driven to ~0) the FBP fixed point is a strong attractor for the data term at ANY stable step -> iter-4 attacks it via tv_lambda_init UP (stronger TV prior gradient to pull off FBP). BUDGET: iter-2 ran ~750s (<1200s wall); identical compute.

DIAGNOSIS of iter-1 (step_init=1e-2): hr=0.0, val_psnr=17.27 dB -- 19 dB WORSE than the LD-FBP baseline (36.32 dB), val_ssim 0.719 vs baseline 0.920. SLURM training log (job 772163) is the smoking gun: loss FROZEN at 0.004813 across ALL 10 epochs and every learned step[k]=0.01 / lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init (only step_9 drifted to 0.00937). FAILURE MODE (named): STEP-TOO-LARGE OVERSHOOT -> saturated-gradient training freeze. Mechanism (docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 + Mayo iter-3): the data gradient R^T(R f - g) uses the RAW unnormalized adjoint of the 128-view breast forward op; tv_step_init=0.01 (inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr) is ~operator-norm too large, so f - 0.01*R^T(...) overshoots into a bad clamped basin at K=1, the clamp/divergence kills the gradient to the 20 log-scalars -> they never move -> recon diverges from FBP regardless of epochs. baseline FBP PSNR=36.32 confirms data/projector are fine; only the unrolled step scale is wrong. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-2 -> 1e-4 (100x smaller; keeps the unrolled iteration INSIDE the stable basin near FBP where gradients flow to the scalars). Historical breast iter-2 (findings 2026-05-23) used exactly step_init=1e-4 and the recon stayed near FBP (loss dropped, scalars departed init). All else IDENTICAL to iter-1 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: at 100x smaller step the training UN-FREEZES -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and val_psnr recovers from 17.3 toward/above the FBP floor (36.3 dB) so hr rises above 0. FALSIFIER: if loss stays flat AND scalars stay pinned, the harness is deeper-broken (then iter-3 attacks init: drop FBP-init / zero-init, or deepen K). BUDGET: iter-1 ran 750s total (<1200s wall); identical compute -> ~750s.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=200, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-1 hr=0.0 (val_rmse 0.00640 > baseline 0.00521 -> recon WORSE than 128-view sparse FBP), val_ssim=0.940, only 197/200 scans reconstructed because the outer_wall=900s cut the loop at per_scene=4.5s. Ceiling holds. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I over-smooths -> recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline; ALSO the per-scene budget was so tight (4.5s) that inner N2I steps were wall-clipped well below n_iter=200, so each val scan was UNDER-fit. (3) ONE KNOB: outer_wall_s 900 -> 1400 (per_scene 4.5s -> 7.0s). Everything else identical to iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: giving each per-image N2I fit ~55% more wall lets n_iter=200 actually complete on all 200 scans; if the iter-1 hr=0 was partly under-fitting rather than pure over-smoothing, more inner steps should DROP val_rmse toward/below baseline (hr>0). If hr stays 0 even fully-fit, that is stronger evidence the ceiling is STRUCTURAL (the FBP self-supervision target itself caps N2I), which is the documented finding. (5) BUDGET: warm-start ep=3 (~130s) + 200 scans * 7.0s = 1400s + figure ~= 26 min... TOO LONG for 30-min wall. Correction: keep outer_wall=1400 but it is the WHOLE val-loop cap, and warm-start is separate; 130+1400 = 25.5 min + ~1 min figure = ~26.5 min < 30 min wall. Fits. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing. Reserved levers: n_iter, pretrain_epochs, unet_c, lr, warm_start on/off.

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-1 (breast_ct, 128-view sparse, mu up to 0.081), FEASIBILITY baseline on the new seed-20260703 val/test split, val_n=200 (full frozen breast val). NO prior iter this run. Unrolled K=10 TV-GD with per-iter learnable step+lambda (20 trainable scalars), supervised-L2 vs clean phantom, init from LD-FBP. Seeded to REPRODUCE the historical breast iter-1 corner (docs/findings.md 2026-05-23: K=10, step_init=1e-2, lambda_init=1e-3, fbp init) so iter-2+ can genuinely explore off a known point. Documented RISK (findings 2026-05-23): FBP init makes the data-fidelity gradient R^T(R*FBP-g)~0, so the learned TV does ~nothing and recon stays at FBP -> hr can plateau at/near 0. The classical (non-learned) tv_iterative sibling reaches hr~0.16 (200 iters) up to 0.355 (1000 iters, lambda~2.5e-3) on this split, so the FBP ceiling is NOT 0 here -- genuine room to explore (init, lambda, K, step, epochs). HYPOTHESIS: a learned per-iter step+lambda schedule lands at or slightly above the FBP baseline (hr>0); if it collapses to ~FBP (hr~0) the FBP-init zero-gradient trap is active and iter-2 attacks it (step size / drop-fbp-init / deeper K). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score): train = 400 samples x 10 epochs x K=10 fwd+bwd; val = 200 slices x K=10 unrolled, val_chunk=5. Classical tv breast iter-1 ran 196s at 200 GD iters over 200 val slices; this variant's train adds ~4-6 min -> est ~8-10 min total, ~2x margin under 1200s wall.

rationale: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=20, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_iter=5000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1000, naf_per_scene_s=48.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 FEASIBILITY (breast-ct-claude-agentic-naf-search-20260703-01, REDONE breast split train3600/val200/test200 seed20260703). GOAL: does naf (Neural Attenuation Field, per-scene self-supervised INR -- one coordinate-MLP optimized PER breast slice against its OWN 128-view sinogram, no training set) run on the redone breast_ct staged val split and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png + recon_raw.npz WITHIN the HARD 20-min budget, scoring under the frozen calibrated-headroom metric (display 0..0.05, mu>=0 floor, FOV-masked)? BUDGET REASONING (load-bearing): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. Per the user hint, naf is HEAVY so I use a SMALL val_n=20 (NOT 200) kept CONSTANT across all 20 iters so they are comparable (breast val load is deterministic first-20 of the 200-case val split). 1000s outer wall / 20 scenes = 48 s/scene (naf_per_scene_s=48), inside the 20-min compute budget with figure+IO headroom before the 30-min sbatch kill. breast is 512x512 at 128 views x det; each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + 128-view fan-beam forward-project + backward. 48 s/scene buys HUNDREDS of steps -- a GENUINE NeRF-style per-scene fit, so hr=0 here would be a STRUCTURAL verdict, NOT budget starvation. naf_n_iter=5000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor. Leaner MLP than default (hidden 192->128, layers 5->4, n_freqs 10->8) for cheaper steps => more steps/scene; naf_lr 5e-3->1e-2 converges faster from the water-mu init in a bounded budget. naf_n_clip=0.05 (sigmoid head out_scale), naf_tv_weight=1e-4 defaults. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense-view (128-angle) breast-CT -- docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 confirms NAF's sin/cos-posenc coordinate-MLP basis is too coarse for dense soft-tissue at 512^2/128-views and cannot beat the ~0.84 breast LD-FBP baseline (hr=0) even at 5x n_iter. Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint on the redone split under the frozen metric -- a real, valid finding (do NOT reduce val_n further or inflate to make NAF look better; hr=0 plateau documents the ceiling for paper section 5.4).

SIX-BOX vs BEST (iter-6 proj_n_bf=1/img_n_bf=7/lr1e-2/lneg1.0 hr=0.2555). (1) PRIOR: lambda_neg lowering HURT (iter-9 lneg0.1=0.2487) -> the negativity penalty is LOAD-BEARING for BFs (a bilateral cannot clamp negatives itself, unlike the DD-UNet); reverted to 1.0. img side fully mapped (depth7, kernel7, lr1e-2 all optimal). The PROJECTION-domain BF is still at its minimal proj_n_bf=1. (2) Failure mode: a single sinogram BF barely denoises the sparse-view sinogram before FBP; streaks that a deeper proj stack could suppress pre-reconstruction survive into the image. (3) ONE KNOB: proj_n_bf 1 -> 3 (best config otherwise). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 3 chained projection BFs denoise the sinogram more before FBP -> fewer streaks -> hr above 0.2555 toward ~0.26-0.27; if flat/down, proj-domain denoising is not the lever (image-domain dominates) and iter-11 pushes proj_kernel or reverts. (5) BUDGET: proj BFs act on the sinogram (smaller than 512x512 image); 3x cheap -> ~130s. (6) Loop continues. Artifacts saved.

rationale: wu_2015-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=1, wu_n_outer=0, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=2, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-3 (one knob vs iter-2). NUMBERS: iter-1 hr=0 (n_bands=6,n_outer=2: RMSE=0.0247); iter-2 hr=0 (n_bands=6,n_outer=0: RMSE=0.401 PSNR=-1.4 -- pure band-split FBP is CATASTROPHICALLY under-scaled). DIAGNOSIS: aliasing_free_fbp normalises the per-band radial sigmoid weights to sum=1 across bands (weights/wsum), but the band filters PARTITION the ramp |f| (they sum to |f|). Weight-summing the band back-projections with weights that sum to 1 AVERAGES them instead of SUMMING -> the recon is scaled down ~1/n_bands at fully-supported inner pixels. The n_outer=2 residual add-back in iter-1 partially rescaled it (RMSE 0.401->0.0247) but never reached the 0.00521 FBP baseline. ONE KNOB: wu_n_bands 6 -> 1 (n_outer stays 0). At n_bands=1 there is a single band, wsum normalisation gives weight=1 everywhere and the single band filter = the FULL |f| ramp, so aliasing_free_fbp degenerates to a plain ramp FBP. HYPOTHESIS: if n_bands=1 gives RMSE ~= the 0.00521 FBP baseline (hr near 0 but val_ssim ~0.92, PSNR ~36) it CONFIRMS the multi-band weight-normalisation mis-scaling is the whole story (the classical Wu band-split is structurally lossy vs baseline on dense 128-view breast data); if instead single-band clears baseline, that is the operating point to refine. Budget: ~4s.

rationale: wu_2015-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=0, wu_motion_range=8, wu_motion_window=2, wu_soft_thresh=0.0015, val_n=200, val_chunk=4, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (one knob vs iter-1). FAILURE MODE: the residual-refinement OUTER LOOP (forward-project the aliasing-free FBP, subtract, feature-preserving-interp the residual to 2x angles, FBP + soft-threshold + add-back) is INJECTING artefacts, not recovering aliasing structure -- on dense 128-view breast data the view-aliasing is mild so the densified residual is mostly error. ONE KNOB: wu_n_outer 2 -> 0 (skips the entire outer loop; returns the pure aliasing-free band-split FBP alone, 0 params). All else = iter-1. HYPOTHESIS: if I remove the residual add-back loop I expect val hr to rise above 0 (RMSE to drop toward/below the 0.00521 baseline) because the band-split aliasing-free FBP alone avoids the mis-estimated residual densification; if the band-split FBP alone still trails plain-FBP baseline, the band-splitting itself (not just the residual loop) is the problem and iter-3 sweeps n_bands. Budget: ~4s recon, trivially <20min.
